name: FamousSparrow APT Targets Azerbaijani Oil and Gas Industry
description: Bitdefender Labs tracked a sophisticated cyber intrusion against an Azerbaijani oil and gas company conducted by the Chinese APT group FamousSparrow. This multi-wave operation, which spanned from late December 2025 through late February 2026, showcased advanced attack techniques particularly focused on exploiting energy infrastructure in the South Caucasus, an area increasingly recognized for its geopolitical importance following significant changes in European energy supply dynamics.

name: FamousSparrow / SparrowDoor -- Legacy Loader (K7UI.dll) | CTI-003
description: Static analysis of SparrowDoor Stage 1 loader component (K7UI.dll) masquerading as K7 Antivirus. PE32 DLL, 32-bit Intel i386. Features reflective DLL injection of Stage 2 (MpSvc.dll), inverted anti-sandbox logic (terminates when IsDebuggerPresent==0), three-table character substitution system for API-free command normalization, and 113 indirect call sites masking runtime API footprint. Sample sourced from ESET malware-ioc. Analysis: SerapHim - CTI-003.

name: Likely more Earth Estries related samples
Blaze's Security Blog: Earth Estries alive and kicking
description:
Earth Estries, an advanced persistent threat (APT) actor linked to China, remains active and has been observed utilizing various implants, including Snappybee (also referred to as Deed RAT) and ShadowPad. In recent operations, Earth Estries has specifically exploited a newly identified vulnerability in WinRAR, a widely used archive management tool. This vulnerability plays a crucial role in their attack methodology, allowing them to execute malicious shellcode on targeted systems.

The steps of their attack flow center around leveraging the WinRAR vulnerability to gain unauthorized access. Once exploited, the actors can deploy their malware implants to establish further control over the compromised environment. The use of various tools such as Snappybee and ShadowPad enables a diverse range of capabilities for the threat actors, facilitating data exfiltration, remote control, and persistent access to the target networks.

name: IOC&TTP - You will always remember this as the day you finally caught FamousSparrow
description:
本次调查显示，一个早前被认为已不活跃的中国关联威胁组织（外界常称其为“FamousSparrow”）重新活跃，并在近期针对多个目标展开网络间谍活动。研究人员在一次事件应急中，于某美国金融领域相关协会以及位于墨西哥的研究机构的网络内，发现了该组织的最新攻击痕迹。
在这次行动中，威胁组织部署了两种新版本的 SparrowDoor 后门，功能和架构上相比旧版本显著增强。它们能够并行处理命令，还具备模块化设计，且首次搭配使用了 ShadowPad 后门（该后门是典型由中国相关攻击者常用的私人售卖型恶意软件）。
本次攻击展现了威胁者在入侵后如何利用多种技术进行持久化、横向移动以及隐藏踪迹，包括滥用旧版 Windows 及 Exchange 漏洞，置入特制加载器进行反射式载入（Reflective Loading），以及通过后门灵活并行执行命令、动态加载插件等方式达到隐蔽、持久和控制力。与此同时，C&C（指挥与控制）配置可以在后门运行期间被更新，以便灵活切换服务器或减少风险暴露。
本次攻击说明了该威胁组织并未停止运作，而是在持续投入资源对自身后门工具（SparrowDoor）进行迭代，并与其他中国相关团伙常用的 ShadowPad 后门相结合，进一步提升了其攻击效率和隐蔽能力。

name: Game of Emperor: Unveiling Long Term Earth Estries Cyber Intrusions
description: Earth Estries, a Chinese APT group, has been aggressively targeting critical sectors globally since 2023. The group employs advanced techniques and multiple backdoors, including GHOSTSPIDER, SNAPPYBEE, and MASOL RAT, to compromise organizations in telecommunications, government, and other industries across various countries. Their sophisticated attacks exploit server vulnerabilities for initial access and use living-off-the-land binaries for lateral movement. Earth Estries has successfully infiltrated over 20 organizations, demonstrating a complex C&C infrastructure and possible shared tools with other Chinese APT groups. The group's operations involve long-term espionage activities, targeting not only critical services but also vendor networks to facilitate broader access.

name: FamousSparrow Via Custom Backdoor
description: ESET researchers have uncovered a new cyberespionage group targeting hotels, governments, and private companies worldwide. FamousSparrow is a group that consider as the only current user of the custom backdoor, SparrowDoor. It also uses two custom versions of Mimikatz. The initial compromise vector used by FamousSparrow and these systems were compromised through vulnerable internet-facing web applications. We believe FamousSparrow exploited known remote code execution vulnerabilities in Microsoft Exchange (including ProxyLogon in March 2021), Microsoft SharePoint and Oracle Opera (business software for hotel management), which were used to drop various malicious samples.
